title: Adaptive microwindow checkpoints for near-real-time quota reconciliation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Reserved capacity tenants and rolling-window quotas occasionally observe incorrect usage balances due to late-arriving events, clock skew across regions, and bursty traffic that escapes micro-batching. Current monthly/daily reset logic is coarse-grained and causes customer-facing over/under-charging or throttling anomalies. Goal: implement an adaptive microwindow checkpointing system that produces frequent, idempotent quota snapshots with deterministic reconciliation paths to correct drift without manual invoices or tenant-impacting rollbacks.
motivation: Prevent customer-impacting quota drift and enable near-real-time reconciliation for reserved pools and rolling windows. Improve billing accuracy, reduce manual invoice adjustments, and allow safe cutovers for cross-region tenant migrations.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha: Initial triage. Reproduced drift scenario in staging by replaying delayed ingest with 2s-90m latencies. Observed 0.7% aggregate reserved pool under-reporting for bursty tenants.
2026-03-03 - Rae: Spike implemented: microwindow producer writes periodic checkpoints every 30s-5m depending on workload, with a write-ahead delta log. Proof-of-concept validated in local cluster.

2026-03-05 - Eng Review: Decided to use epoch tokens derived from tenant lease + region to ensure idempotent application. Trade-off: more frequent checkpoints increase writes to ledger KVS; we will batch smaller checkpoints and compress deltas.
2026-03-06 - PM Feedback (Jon): Ensure customer-visible audit trail for any retroactive reconciliations and automatic invoice notes for corrected amounts > $50. Add labels to telemetry and alerting.
2026-03-08 - Security: Confirmed encryption-at-rest for checkpoint payloads and KMS policy required for ledger service access. Security review required: true.

2026-03-09 - Perf: Synthetic load tests show checkpoint write latency P95 120ms with current Redis cluster; projected cost increase ~0.9% for heavy tenants. Need to validate Cassandra-backed ledger for scale.
2026-03-10 - Action: Opened follow-up ticket for KVS scaling and retention policy: ENG-813580 (linked). Preparing canary rollout plan for one reserved pool.
Outstanding blockers: KVS throughput limits during global surge, backup/restore compatibility for new checkpoint format, and UX for invoice reconciliation notes.
decision_log: Use epoch-based checkpoint tokens to guarantee idempotency and avoid double-apply during replay.
Maintain both delta log and compacted snapshot to bound reconciliation window and storage.
Introduce adaptive frequency: sample tenant request QPS and increase checkpoint rate for high-burst tenants to minimize drift.
Provide a read-only shadow reconciliation endpoint to preview changes before applying to live balances.
Retroactive adjustments must be accompanied by an audit event and optional invoice-note if monetary delta exceeds threshold.
Rollout in three phases: internal staging, canary on single reserved pool, fleetwide with throttled backlog replay.
Monitor key metrics: checkpoint_apply_lag, cumulative_drift_tokens, reconciliation_actions_per_hour, failed_checkpoint_rate.
Fallback: if ledger KVS overwhelmed, degrade to less-frequent checkpoints and start bulk reconciliation windowing with tenant-aware backoff.
acceptance_criteria: Microwindow checkpoints emitted and stored with epoch tokens and compacted snapshots for sampled tenants in staging.
Reconciliation run can idempotently reapply deltas and converge ledger balance to source-of-truth within 5 minutes for 99th percentile of test cases.
No customer-facing throttling or billing inconsistencies introduced during canary run for target reserved pool.
Telemetry dashboards updated and alerts configured for drift > 0.5% of pool capacity or checkpoint_failure_rate > 0.5%.
Security review completed and KMS access controls enforced for checkpoint ingestion path.
Runbook for manual remediation and invoice annotation documented and reviewed by Finance and Support.
Performance: additional write amplification cost remains under 2% for typical monthly ledger size in prod projection.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Staging: Deploy checkpoint producer/consumer to staging, run synthetic late events for 48h, validate convergence.
Phase 2 - Canary: Enable for a single low-risk reserved pool for 2 weeks, monitor metrics and customer impact, run reconciliation smoke tests.
Phase 3 - Scale: Expand to top 10 reserved pools, enable adaptive frequency, tune KVS retention and compaction windows.
Phase 4 - Fleet: Global rollout with gradual ramp, runbook ready, finance notified for invoice-note automation.
Rollback: Disable checkpoint consumer and revert to prior snapshot epoch; run reconciliation to previous stable checkpoint if drift > safety threshold.
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative on automatic retroactive charging: any monetary change above the threshold will require finance-approved invoice note and optional customer opt-out. Long-term goal is to make reconciliations transparent in Console with per-route audit trails.
